affectedPublicSurfaces: none — test infrastructure only. No product code, no route, no migration, no runtime path.
It is the evidence substrate for the remaining W7-bis slices, which do reach production behaviour.

journeys.name: a-shop-scoped-session-reads-its-own-tenant-and-not-the-other
assertions: as juli_app with tenant A's shop context, rows belonging to A are returned
the same session returns ZERO of tenant B's rows
both halves on the same fixture, so a deny-all cannot pass as isolation
the positive control is asserted first, because 'denied' and 'empty' are otherwise indistinguishable

journeys.name: shop-scope-cannot-reach-user-keyed-tables
assertions: a shop-scoped session reads zero rows from public.users
a shop-scoped session reads zero rows from public.shops
closes the two acceptance criteria #1478 deferred for want of this fixture

journeys.name: the-seeder-covers-what-it-claims
assertions: every table the seeder names has at least one row for the tenant it seeded
the claim is asserted from the database rather than stated in a docstring — the helper this extends claimed 'all tenant-scoped tables' and seeded three

migrationCompatibility.notes: No migration and no product code. The fixture seeds rows into an isolated database, which is why the consuming module joins _ISOLATED_DATABASE_MODULES: test_rls_policies.py was isolated for asserting unscoped global counts (#1425), and seeded rows would otherwise leak into that class of assertion.

rollbackAssertion.postCutoverFailureBehavior: nothing deployed changes; reverting removes a test fixture and the three remaining W7-bis slices lose their evidence substrate.

doNotInfer: Do not build this on tests/integration/conftest.py's `engine`/`session` fixtures. They are SQLite in-memory with a schema_translate_map, and SQLite cannot express roles, RLS or row locks — anything built on them proves nothing about isolation.

Do not try to connect as juli_app with a password. The role is NOLOGIN in CI by design (ADR-086 decision 7); `SET ROLE juli_app` on a superuser connection is how RLS is applied, and it is what #1329's proof already does.

Do not assert only the denial. A session that can read nothing at all passes a denial-only test and fails the feature. The positive control — reading the tenant's own rows — is what separates isolation from deny-all, and it is the exact failure mode ADR-089 exists for.
Do not trust the seeder's docstring. The helper this extends claimed to seed 'across all tenant-scoped tables' and seeded three; coverage is asserted from the database instead.

Do not seed into the shared database. test_rls_policies.py was isolated for asserting unscoped global counts (#1425); seeded rows would leak into that class of assertion from any module that shares the database.
